USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the May 19 tariff pause in place and send Ross to Beijing to convert the vague joint statement into dated, sector-specific purchase contracts—while refusing to treat those purchases as a substitute for structural IP/tech-transfer remedies. Do not impose the Section 301 list this week and do not lift the ZTE denial order except as a conditioned, paid enforcement settlement (fines, management change, compliance monitors). Keep the published $50B list, investment-restriction track, and export-control tools explicitly in reserve if China will not move beyond a communiqué.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a mild opportunity, not a crisis. The U.S. opened this dispute from a position of strength: the March 22 Section 301 findings and April 3 ~$50B list put China on the defensive; the April 16 ZTE denial order created firm-level leverage that Beijing is now trying to unwind; and after Washington talks China agreed only to “significantly increase” purchases, with Mnuchin declaring the trade war “on hold” while Lighthizer publicly reserved tariffs, investment restrictions, and export regulations because forced technology transfer, cyber theft, and innovation protection remain unresolved. U.S. macros as of late May do not show a trade-war recession: Michigan sentiment is still ~98, industrial production is above late-2017 levels, VIX has compressed to ~12.6 after the March/April tariff scare, and the goods deficit actually narrowed in the latest print. Offsets that keep the reading far from a slam-dunk: China already hit ~$3B of U.S. farm goods (April 2) and tabled a matching ~$50B list aimed at soybeans, autos, and aircraft (April 4); U.S. goods exports to China have fallen sharply in the window; and the May 19 text has no dollar figure, no enforcement clock, and only a promise to “strengthen cooperation” on IP—exactly the purchase-for-structure swap Schumer and Lighthizer warned against. That mix justifies negotiate at 0, not escalate (which would blow up a framework five days old and invite the farm-belt hit before talks are tested) and not concede_purchases/partial_rollback (which would cash ZTE and the 301 list for an unenforceable communiqué).
key_factors: May 19 joint statement is a pause, not a deal: no $200B figure, no enforcement clock, IP language is hortatory
ZTE denial order is the sharpest live U.S. lever; lifting it cheaply would signal weakness to Xi and to Congress
Section 301 structural agenda (forced tech transfer, cyber theft, licensing) remains the core U.S. interest and is still unmet
U.S. real economy is not yet paying a material trade-war price (sentiment, IP, VIX, deficit)
China’s $50B retaliation list concentrates pain on soy, autos, and aircraft—reason not to re-escalate this week
Internal U.S. split (Mnuchin pause vs Lighthizer reserve tools) argues for holding leverage while negotiating specifics

sources_cited.excerpt: US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold." Markets rally.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.

USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
China imposes retaliatory tariffs on about $3B of US goods (pork, fruit, nuts, wine, and related items) in response to Section 232 steel/aluminum tariffs.

Mnuchin: tariffs on hold while executing the framework; Lighthizer: purchases are secondary to forced technology transfers, cyber theft and innovation protection; statement has no dollar amount and is 'too vague to be binding.'

Joint statement omitted the $200B deficit-cut target; Lighthizer reserved tariffs, investment restrictions and export regulations; Schumer warned a ZTE capitulation plus purchase promises would signal weakness.
Reports of a possible ZTE deal: lift the sales ban in exchange for management/board changes and fines; China also floated removing some farm tariffs.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment latest 98 (May 2018), still elevated versus late 2017.
VIX closed 12.58 on 2018-05-23 after the March/April tariff spike, indicating markets priced a pause not a crisis.
U.S. goods exports to China down about 24% from Dec 2017 to May 2018, showing farm/export exposure even before the $50B lists take effect.
U.S. goods trade deficit narrowed to -$66.6B in May 2018 from -$71.4B in Dec 2017 — no evidence yet of a trade-war blowout.
